everything.name: Themed Skin Pack
everything.validation: Publish free version on Planet Minecraft; iterate on feedback
everything.intent_and_origin: Lowest barrier to entry for Marketplace. Proves pixel art consistency, manifest correctness, slim/classic handling, and packaging discipline. Reviewers expect at least one polished skin pack in portfolio. Theme should target underserved niche (e.g., 'Retro-Future Workers', 'Cryptid Hunters', 'Eco-Engineers') rather than generic anime/character packs.
everything.design_objective: Create 12 themed skins (6 classic + 6 slim) with 3 variants each = 36 texture files. Resource pack only (type: 'resources'). Manifest with unique UUIDs, correct versioning. Test on Steve/Alex models, verify no Z-fighting. Price tier: 160-320 Minecoins (~$0.64-$1.28 creator). Build in Blockbench skin template, package via Bridge.
everything.my_analysis_and_suggestions: UX Strategy: Skin packs are impulse buys — trailer must show all variants in 15 seconds. Monetization: Volume game; 100 sales at 320 coins = $128. Differentiation: Pick a cohesive visual theme with clear silhouette language. Avoid saturated markets (anime, superhero, generic 'cool'). Use outer layer for hats/accessories. Document theme research in design doc.

everything.name: 64x Texture Pack
sources: Microsoft Learn: Resource Packs, Models, Materials
everything.validation: Release beta on MCPEDL/Planet Minecraft; collect performance reports from mobile users
everything.intent_and_origin: Proves texture artistry at scale, geometry system mastery, material/render pipeline, and performance awareness. Reviewers look for: full vanilla coverage, custom models (not just reskins), connected textures, and cohesive art direction. Theme must be visually distinct — not 'faithful' or 'default+' which are saturated.
everything.design_objective: Full block/item/entity retexture at 64x (128x for hero blocks). 3+ custom block models via Blockbench (.geo.json + UV atlas). Custom materials: emissive, transparency, animated textures. Render controllers for state-based variants. Connected textures via model permutations. Resource pack only. Price tier: 320-660 Minecoins (~$1.28-$2.64 creator). Target underserved themes: Paper Craft, Neon Noir, Biomechanical.
everything.my_analysis_and_suggestions: UX Strategy: Texture packs are 'live with it' purchases — screenshots must show world context, not just block grids. Monetization: Recurring buyers; faithful packs have longest tail. Differentiation: Invest in custom models for 3-5 signature blocks (furnace, crafting table, enchanting table) that players see constantly. Use texture atlases for performance. Test on Android/iOS for memory/load times.

everything.name: Scripted Micro-Add-On
sources: Microsoft Learn: Script API, Molang, Custom Entities/Blocks
everything.validation: Open-source core mechanic on GitHub; invite code review from Bridge Discord
everything.intent_and_origin: The single most important technical proof for reviewers. Demonstrates Script API fluency, component architecture, event-driven design, tick budget discipline, and gameplay UI/UX. Must be a complete, polished mechanic — not a tech demo. Concept should be instantly understandable: 'Grappling Hook', 'Portable Workbench', or 'Pet Companion'.
everything.design_objective: Behavior + Resource + Scripts pack. TypeScript entry (scripts/main.ts → compiled JS). 1 custom entity (components, events, animation controller) + 1 custom block (components, permutations, block entity for storage) + 1 scripted system. Molang in animations/render controllers. Custom UI via @minecraft/server-ui (ActionFormData). Tick profiling: stay under 50ms. Price tier: 660-1,720+ Minecoins (~$2.64-$6.88+ creator).
everything.my_analysis_and_suggestions: UX Strategy: Scripted add-ons need in-game tutorial — first 30 seconds must teach mechanic without text walls. Monetization: Higher price point but lower volume; relies on YouTube showcases. Differentiation: Pick a mechanic that feels 'impossible in vanilla' but fits Bedrock's sandbox (physics, inventory, companion AI). Document architecture in design doc: component diagram, event flow, tick budget breakdown. This is your engineering portfolio piece.

everything.name: Adventure Map
sources: Microsoft Learn: Commands, NPCs, Structure Blocks, Loot Tables
Community map design principles (Planet Minecraft featured maps)
everything.validation: Recruit 3+ playtesters via Discord; collect completion times, stuck points, fun ratings (1-10)
everything.intent_and_origin: Proves level design, pacing, command/function mastery, player onboarding without tutorials, and replayability design. Reviewers want to see: clear progression, fair challenge, no softlocks, and a satisfying 30-45 minute experience. Genre should showcase systems thinking (puzzle, parkour, or narrative mystery).
everything.design_objective: World Template + Behavior Pack. Built in Bedrock Editor → export via Structure Blocks (.mcstructure). Behavior pack: function files (.mcfunction) for progression, commands for mechanics. NPCs with dialogue trees, command triggers, reward dispensing. Loot tables for chests; trade tables for vendors. Scoreboard/objectives for progression. Playtest report with 3+ testers. Price tier: 490-1,340 Minecoins (~$1.96-$5.36 creator).
everything.my_analysis_and_suggestions: UX Strategy: First 2 minutes must establish goal, controls, and hook — no text dumps. Use environmental storytelling. Monetization: Maps are 'one-and-done' but drive reviews and portfolio depth. Differentiation: Design around a single core mechanic that escalates (puzzle: new redstone logic per room; parkour: new movement tech per floor; narrative: new clue type per chapter). Document level flow diagram in design doc.

everything.name: Capstone Mini Mash-up
everything.validation: Full test matrix: Win10, Android, iOS, Xbox Dev Mode. Performance budget: <30ms tick mobile, <100MB RAM
everything.intent_and_origin: Integration test of all skills — the 'final exam'. Must prove end-to-end delivery, cross-system integration, performance budgeting, commercial polish, and project management. Everything must work together without conflicts: world depends on custom blocks/entities, texture pack reskins vanilla + custom consistently, skins match world theme, scripted system integrated into progression.
everything.design_objective: World + Texture Pack (32x) + 2 Skins + 1 Scripted System. All custom content interdependent. Notion/GitHub Projects board with epics: World, Texture, Skins, Script, Integration, Polish, Test, Docs. Weekly milestones: W27-28 blockout, W29-32 systems, W33-36 art pass, W37-38 integration, W39-40 polish. Price tier: 990-2,500+ Minecoins (~$3.96-$10+ creator). Flagship quality.
everything.my_analysis_and_suggestions: UX Strategy: This is your 'flagship' — trailer production value matters. Monetization: Highest single-pack revenue potential; also drives cross-sales to other packs. Differentiation: Theme must unify all systems (e.g., 'Cyberpunk Heist' world + neon texture + hacker skins + grappling hook script). Document integration architecture: dependency graph, shared assets, conflict resolution. This proves you can ship a commercial product, not just tech demos.

top_20_quick_start.name: Themed Skin Pack
top_20_quick_start.why_first: Lowest risk, fastest feedback loop, proves art pipeline + manifest discipline. Required portfolio piece.

top_20_quick_start.name: 64x Texture Pack
top_20_quick_start.why_first: Runs parallel to Skin Pack; proves geometry/material pipeline. Different skill set from skins.

top_20_quick_start.name: Scripted Micro-Add-On
top_20_quick_start.why_first: Critical technical proof. Sequential bottleneck — start after Skin Pack foundation.

design_patterns.name: Parallel Art Tracks
design_patterns.description: Skins and Textures are pure art — run them simultaneously. Scripting is sequential bottleneck. Maximizes calendar efficiency.

design_patterns.name: Dossier-Driven Development
design_patterns.description: Write the project dossier (tagline, features, test plan) BEFORE building. Forces scope clarity and reviewer empathy.

design_patterns.name: Public Beta on Free Platforms
design_patterns.description: Release early versions on Planet Minecraft/MCPEDL. Free QA, community building, and portfolio evidence of iteration.

design_patterns.name: Content Calendar as Accountability
design_patterns.description: Weekly devlog + 3 Shorts + 5 Tweets = forced progress. Audience becomes stakeholder; algorithm rewards consistency.

design_patterns.name: Theme-First, Mechanics-Second
design_patterns.description: Pick underserved visual themes first (Retro-Future, Neon Noir, Biomechanical). Mechanics serve theme, not vice versa. Easier marketing.

design_patterns.name: Performance Budget from Day 1
design_patterns.description: Target <30ms tick on mobile, <100MB RAM. Profile every session. Mobile-first prevents certification rejection.

design_patterns.name: Documentation as Product
design_patterns.description: Design docs, test reports, architecture diagrams are portfolio pieces. Reviewers read them; employers value them.

design_patterns.name: Cross-Pack Integration Design
design_patterns.description: Capstone isn't 'one more pack' — it's the integration test. Design dependencies between packs from Month 1 (shared palette, shared systems).

design_patterns.name: Reviewer Empathy
design_patterns.description: Reviewers spend ~2 min per project. Dossier must be scannable: tagline, trailer, screenshots, tech badges, test report, checklist. No walls of text.
